findings.ref: EFF-08 (owner decision 2026-11-21), EFF-18 п.5, EFF-25, EFF-27; threat path 'idempotency key of another requester in the same tenant'
findings.problem: Idempotency is per requester since 0003, but the provider idempotency key is still the bare idempotency_key. Two requesters of one tenant with the same key get two intents; the second reaches the provider with the same (tenant, key), the provider returns the first receipt (outcome duplicate), the connector reports succeeded, and the second intent ends succeeded with the first intent's provider_operation_id. The second approved message (other recipient, other text) is never sent. An agent that knows Signals' key format (signals:<candidate>:v<n>) suppresses Signals' approved effects this way: the squatting path the owner decision was meant to close is moved to the effect, and now silent. Reconcile by idempotency_key (EFF-25) would do the same
findings.reproduction: test_executor.py stack; grants and auto policy for agent:t-alpha:actor and agent:t-alpha:reader on a-public; propose by both with idempotency_key 'shared-key-1' (texts differ, recipients partner_1/partner_2); drain -> statuses (succeeded, succeeded); provider journal [(A, partner_1, ok), (B, partner_2, duplicate)]; both executions provider_operation_id demo-op-82a0b67c-...
findings.required_improvement: Provider idempotency key unique per (tenant, requester, key): the connector derives it from the token (e.g. f"{claims['req']}/{claims['idk']}" or SHA-256 of both) and passes it to the provider and to reconcile; the fake provider journal keeps the intent's idempotency_key column for AC-M8-01/08; one sentence in EFF-18 п.5. Test on the real stack: the reproduction above -> 2 provider effects with 2 different operation ids, both intents succeeded; AC-M8-08 retries still share one provider key
